message.content:
{
  "backend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Implementation instructions for backend engineers (do not rename DB column 'title'; enforce request rejection; remove title from public responses):

1) Scope identification
   - Locate all public API response serializers/DTOs/transformers and the OpenAPI/JSON Schema or equivalent public API specs that are used to produce responses for clients (both list and single-entry endpoints).
   - Treat “public responses” as the entire externally documented API surface. Do not change internal/private admin/internal-only endpoints unless explicitly confirmed.

2) Response changes
   - Remove the title field from every public response schema/serializer/DTO. Ensure the returned objects still include name, id, description, owner_id, created_at (unchanged).
   - Ensure mapping code from the database entity to the public DTO does not copy or expose the title property. Keep the underlying DB column/property named title (do not rename or drop it).
   - Update the public OpenAPI/JSON Schema/spec to reflect the absence of title in responses.

3) Request validation / rejection
   - Update request validation for all public endpoints that accept entry payloads (create/update etc.) so that any incoming JSON body containing the title field results in HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity.
   - Use the existing API error format (do not invent a new error schema). The acceptance condition only requires status 422; tests should also assert that the error references the unexpected title field if your project’s error format does so.

4) Tests
   - Add or update unit and integration tests to assert:
     a) Public responses do not contain title and do contain name, id, description, owner_id, created_at.
     b) Sending a request payload that includes title returns HTTP 422.
   - Add contract tests for the public API (schema validation) ensuring response schemas no longer include title.

5) Docs and changelog
   - Update public API docs/spec to remove title from responses and document that sending title in requests will result in 422.

6) Rollout / coordination (required):
   - Because the backend will reject requests that include title, coordinate deployment with frontend team: deploy frontend changes that stop sending title first, verify production traffic contains no title, then deploy backend changes that remove title from responses and enforce 422.
   - During rollout, add logging/monitoring to detect any incoming requests that still include title so teams can quickly remediate stray clients.

7) Backwards-compatibility note
   - Do not accept or silently ignore title in public requests; the requirement mandates returning 422. Do not change DB column name or internal storage.

8) Acceptance tests to run before marking done
   - Automated test suite: response schema checks (no title), request-with-title returns 422.
   - End-to-end test: frontend updated build communicates with backend in staging — verify UI shows name and not title and no requests include title. Monitor logs for incoming title-containing requests.

9) Minimal implementation checklist to commit
   - Remove title from all public serializers/DTOs and API specs.
   - Add validation rule rejecting title in request bodies with HTTP 422.
   - Add/modify tests described above.
   - Add monitoring for unexpected title in incoming requests.
   - Coordinate deployment ordering with frontend as described."
  },
  "frontend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Implementation instructions for frontend engineers (remove fallback reading title; stop sending title to backend):

1) Code changes
   - Identify every place where UI code reads entry.title as a fallback or primary display value and remove that usage. Ensure all UI display and logic use entry.name instead.
   - Remove any fallback logic that attempted to read title when name was missing. The public responses will not include title; rely on name being present.
   - Update TypeScript/Flow/PropTypes/interfaces/types to remove title from the client-facing response type, or mark it as internal-only if your codebase distinguishes internal vs public types. Do not assume the backend renamed the DB column.

2) Outgoing requests
   - Audit all client-side create/update payload builders and ensure they do not include a title property. Ensure serializers that produce request bodies omit title.
   - Add a build-time lint or unit test that fails if any outgoing request payload includes title (prevent regressions).

3) Error handling
   - Keep existing generic request error handling. Add a specific test/assertion to ensure when backend returns HTTP 422 (due to title present), the UI surfaces an appropriate error to the user using the existing error UI/format. Do not invent a new error format.

4) Tests
   - Update unit and integration tests to assert:
     a) Components render entry.name and do not rely on entry.title.
     b) Client requests do not include title.
     c) When backend returns 422 (simulate response that indicates title was present), the UI handles it gracefully using existing error handling.

5) Coordination / deployment (required)
   - Deploy these frontend changes before the backend change that will begin rejecting title-containing requests. Verify in staging and production that no outgoing requests include title before the backend rollout.
   - Add temporary runtime logging to detect if any code path still includes title in requests during the rollout window; remove logging once rollout is complete and verified.

6) Docs and tests
   - Update any client-side API contracts or generated client code to reflect that public responses do not include title.
   - Add e2e test that exercises list and single-entry views to verify UI shows name, no title present, and backend responses still include id/description/owner_id/created_at.

7) Minimal implementation checklist to commit
   - Remove uses of entry.title in rendering/fallbacks.
   - Update client types to drop title from public response shape.
   - Ensure no outgoing requests include title; add lint/test to enforce.
   - Add/modify tests for 422 handling and display of name.
   - Coordinate deployment ordering with backend and monitor for stray requests including title."
  }
}
